findings.headline: 8 of 11 documented 99215s (73%) in a random sample are documented below the billed level; peer rate is 8%
findings.interpretation: Bills 99215 on 27% of claims, against 2.4% expected for this panel (risk-adjusted z 8.8). 61% of the 99215s are for patients with 0-1 chronic conditions. In the random sample of 30, 9 charts were below the billed level. Draft overpayment estimate from the sample: $2,253 (CI $1,503-$3,003). A certified coder should re-score the charts.

findings.headline: 4 of 10 documented 99215s (40%) are below the billed level; peer rate is 8%
findings.interpretation: Bills 99215 on 15.5% of claims, against 2.2% expected (risk-adjusted z 4.86). 65% of the 99215s are for low-complexity patients. Weaker than 1000000120: the overall below-level rate (13%) did not trigger the chart rule. Draft estimate from the random sample: $592 (CI $240-$943). A modest case that needs coder review.

findings.headline: Charts support the billed levels, but the notes look inflated: 30% claim data review with no test on the claim; the audit trail shows bulk-created and paste-heavy notes
findings.interpretation: Bills 99215 on 24% of claims, against 2.6% expected (risk-adjusted z 7.5), and the panel is mostly low complexity. No chart was below the billed level. However, 53% of notes address fewer problems than the claimed level implies, 27% describe data review the claims cannot back, 17% are duplicates, and the audit trail shows 10% bulk-created and 7% paste-heavy notes. That suggests documentation written to match the bill, but these are rates, not proof. Recommend a human coder and audit-trail review before any leaning.

findings.headline: 99215 share is about 9 times expected, but a random sample of 30 charts mostly supports the billed levels (2 of 30 below)
findings.interpretation: Note signals are within the normal range. The charts do not support upcoding, and the low-complexity panel does not explain the share. Monitor.

findings.headline: 99215 share is 5.3 times expected; 1 of 30 random charts below the billed level
findings.interpretation: Documentation supports the billed levels. 17% of notes describe data review with no test on the claim, which is a mild signal. No upcoding finding.

findings.headline: 99215 share is 4.4 times expected; 0 of 30 charts below the billed level, but 33% of notes are duplicates
findings.interpretation: The charts support billing. The high duplicate-note rate could be copy-forward, which honest practices also do. Optional audit-trail review.

findings.headline: 99215 share is 3.6 times expected; 0 of 43 charts (random plus targeted 99215) below the billed level
findings.interpretation: The 99215 documentation supports billing. 7 targeted visits were not returned, which is not evidence either way. No upcoding finding.

findings.headline: 99215 share is 6.4 times expected; 3 of 50 charts (random plus targeted 99215) below the billed level
findings.interpretation: The below-level rate is in line with peers (8%) and the note signals are unremarkable. The excess 99215 share is unexplained, but the charts do not support upcoding.

findings.headline: High-volume practice with a sicker panel; 99215 share rises with complexity, and 4 of 49 charts are below the billed level (8%, the peer rate)
findings.interpretation: 99215 share is 2.4 times expected. The share climbs from 4% for patients with 0 conditions to 35% for patients with 5 or more, and the documentation supports the billed levels.

findings.headline: Highest screen score (risk-adjusted z 10.1); 99215 share is high even for patients with 0-1 conditions; no records received
findings.interpretation: The claims pattern is concerning: 23-26% 99215 on low-complexity patients, against 2-3% for peers. The office asked for an extension and then did not respond. Non-response is not evidence of upcoding, so the provider cannot be judged from charts. Recommend a renewed request later.

findings.headline: 99215 share is 5.9 times expected; no records received
findings.interpretation: The office asked for an extension and then did not respond. The request is closed without inference.

findings.headline: 99215 share is 4.6 times expected but rises with patient complexity (64% for patients with 5+ conditions); records request drew a scope objection and then no response
